definition: TorchAudio is PyTorch’s audio package: loading audio, spectrograms, resampling and pretrained speech models.
details: Part of the PyTorch project at Meta, maintained by the PyTorch Foundation.

explainer.lead: How to install TorchAudio, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.

quickstart.python:
import torchaudio

waveform, sr = torchaudio.load("speech.wav")
mel = torchaudio.transforms.MelSpectrogram(sample_rate=sr, n_mels=80)(waveform)
print(waveform.shape, mel.shape)

explainer.inAi: Turn raw audio into the mel spectrograms speech and audio models expect.
explainer.jsNote: TorchAudio is a Python library with no official JavaScript or TypeScript package; call it from a Python service if your app is written in JavaScript.

tiers.eli5: If PyTorch is a workshop, TorchAudio is the audio drawer: it holds the tools for loading sounds, turning them into pictures of sound, changing their speed, and using speech models already built for you.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers reach for it to load audio, compute spectrograms, resample and use pretrained speech models without assembling those pieces themselves. It is part of the PyTorch project at Meta and maintained by the PyTorch Foundation.
tiers.paperLevel: TorchAudio is PyTorch's audio package, providing audio loading, spectrograms, resampling and pretrained speech models. It is part of the PyTorch project at Meta, maintained by the PyTorch Foundation.

explainer.example: A speech pipeline loads a clip, converts it to a spectrogram and runs a pretrained speech model, all through TorchAudio.
